questions: This applicant has diagnosed sleep apnea with documented CPAP compliance. Section 13 charges 50 for diagnosed sleep apnea but refers treated sleep-disordered breathing to judgement. With documented CPAP compliance, is the 50 debit charged in full, reduced to a smaller figure, or removed altogether?

This applicant's liver enzymes are elevated but below twice the upper limit of normal, with no alcohol history and no treatment. Section 12 charges 25 for elevated liver enzymes but refers borderline liver chemistry to judgement. Is an elevation under twice the upper limit of normal treated as borderline, and if so is the 25 debit still charged, waived, or is the file postponed for repeat labs?

This applicant is a class C high-voltage lineman (50 debits) who also competes in club saloon racing, 14 events a year (amateur motorsport flat extra of $5.00 per $1,000). Section 10 refers a hazardous occupation appearing together with a hazardous avocation to judgement. Are the class C debit and the motorsport flat extra both applied as they stand, or does the combination change the debit total, the flat extra band, or the decision?

Section 15 allows an exclusion rider naming one hazard at no charge but does not say when it is used instead of a flat extra. For this applicant's club saloon racing at 14 events a year, is the $5.00 per $1,000 flat extra the correct modifier, or should the motorsport hazard be excluded by rider instead?
